title: Seven layers of a production agent: AWS Pluggable Agentic AI Framework
caption:
Your agent demo works. Production is a different question.

AWS just published a seven-layer reference architecture for taking multi-agent apps on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore from prototype to production. It is vendor guidance, not a standard, and the services it names are examples you can swap.

The seven layers, one swipe each:
1. Data and Knowledge
2. Model and Inference
3. Orchestration
4. Security and Guardrails
5. Application
6. Observability
7. Agentic Operations

My favourite idea: stable contracts between layers, so you can change one technology without rebuilding the rest.

Save this as a checklist for your next agent design review. Which layer does your team skip first? Tell me in the comments.

Source: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/pluggable-agentic-ai-framework-a-seven-layer-composable-enterprise-agentic-ai-reference-architecture-on-amazon-bedrock-agentcore/

slides.headline: 7 layers between your agent demo and ==production.==
slides.sub: AWS's Pluggable Agentic AI Framework, one layer per slide.

slides.title: 1. Data and Knowledge
paragraphs: An agent is only as good as the data it can reach.
The layer's contract: **accept a query, return the most relevant information** as context for the agent.
slides.callout: Examples: Bedrock Knowledge Bases, S3 Vectors, DynamoDB.

slides.title: 2. Model and Inference
paragraphs: Pick models by **configuration, not hardwired code**. Small, fast models for simple tasks, larger ones for nuanced reasoning.
A routing layer keeps agents decoupled from provider APIs.
slides.callout: Example: a LiteLLM proxy as the common interface.

slides.title: 3. Orchestration
paragraphs: Simple task: one agent. Cross-domain work: a **supervisor delegating to scoped specialists**.
Specialists run only with the tools they are granted. Discover them through a central agent registry.
slides.callout: Examples: Strands Agents, AgentCore Gateway, MCP and A2A.

slides.title: 4. Security and Guardrails
paragraphs: Built in from **day one**. Treat external content as untrusted and authenticate every request.
Use scoped, temporary credentials, mask PII, keep an audit trail, and add human approval for high-impact actions.
slides.callout: Examples: AgentCore Identity and Policy, Bedrock Guardrails.

slides.title: 5. Application
paragraphs: Where the user experience lives: chat, API or widget.
Keep it **intentionally thin**. Present the conversation, pass requests down, and put no business logic here.
Design interfaces other agents can call too.

slides.title: 6. Observability
paragraphs: Watch every layer from day one, not after the first incident.
Collect **end-to-end traces**, cost and tokens per request, time to first token, and dashboards for latency, errors and spend.

slides.title: 7. Agentic Operations
paragraphs: The layer that **closes the loop** after launch.
AWS says to set it up from day one, so you can show the agent still works after every release, not only at launch.

slides.sub: Vendor guidance from AWS. Services shown are examples, swap them freely.
